techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk. Demonstrated specifically ON Spear (BirdOfQin, 2024-10-09): "I'm using a medium armor class (Spear) and my block value isn't even fazed by the fortes."

gameplay.text: The spear is a polearm ubiquitous to warfare throughout the ages. In Conqueror's Blade, spear users have excellent mounted attack capabilities and the ability to deal great burst damage to enemy heroes. However, they have little ability to inflict control effects and are severely weakened without access to mounts.

roleLabel: Spear users have excellent mounted attack capabilities and the ability to deal great burst damage to enemy heroes.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.text: Look for undefended prey; poke from horseback to bait cooldowns before committing to a dismount engage.

Support your own units when engaging - diving into blobs on horseback or over-committing to Hurricane's Edge can get you destroyed. Focus on maximizing hero-and-unit synergy (cav / exo / static units / standalone units, etc.) rather than freelancing.

Brace-tank niche: can walk into braced units (Forte, Halberds, Phalanx) at minimal range with block value effectively unfazed - flagged by its own source as a niche/outnumbered-enemy scenario, not a general frontline tactic.
Piercing Damage is the top-priority weapon stat - "like oxygen, maximize this".
Assisted Aiming on Hero is a deliberate tradeoff, not a strict upgrade.

bullets.lead: Lugh's March's block-during-cast carries a hidden risk:
bullets.text: if your block breaks mid-animation and you're hit again, you can get stunned unexpectedly.
Procris's Gift is the go-to tool for finishing exos hiding behind blobs in stalemate fights (roughly 3-5 hits per Amya's estimate).
use the horseback right-click attack to provoke enemy cooldowns before committing to a dismount.

Walking (not sprinting) into a braced unit's minimal range takes markedly less brace damage, because brace damage scales with the attacker's speed relative to the braced unit - verified on Spear specifically by BirdOfQin's clip.

experienced players on OTHER classes actively hold their block specifically to play around Spear's Procris's Gift - treat this as a proxy signal that landing it clean against aware opponents is competitive, not free damage.

aimingNotes.assistedAimHero: Yes: won't miss a dismount when close enough to the target; may dismount on a wall and fall off if an enemy is below; can't turn around for a back-attack dismount without deliberately looking for the target's back first. No: can rotate the camera during the dismount to chase the target's back with more precision (requires skill); won't get mis-placed on landing; takes time to master but more rewarding in the long run.
